s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain and systemic inflammation with rapid deterioration and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Diffuse papules on trunk and extremities
Rapid deterioration requiring intubation and vasopressors
key_facts: Male toddler presented to the emergency department
Abdominal pain and distention of 1 day's duration
Fever and vomiting of 1 day's duration
Bruises on both flanks
Diffuse papules on trunk and extremities developed over 2 days
Condition rapidly deteriorated
Required intubation, vasopressors, and empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics
Hyponatremia and neutropenia present
Elevated liver enzymes (AST: 45 U/L, ALT: 142 U/L)
Elevated C-reactive protein (>270 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (43 mm/h)
Ferritin level: 603 ng/mL
Proteinuria and hematuria on urinalysis
Cavitary lesions in lungs on CT chest/abdomen
Areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys on CT chest/abdomen
Multifocal lesions on MRI brain
Punch biopsy showed small organisms within vasculature and large neutrophilic pustule with inflammation
Tissue Gram staining showed Gram-positive cocci in vessels
Tissue culture, blood culture, bronchial washings, and fluid from bilateral empyemas all showed positive results

shortlist.label: Purpura fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with purpuric retiform patches and rapid deterioration, consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of sepsis, including fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed Gram-positive cocci in vessels

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of toxic shock syndrome, including fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Meningococcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of sepsis, including fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed Gram-positive cocci in vessels

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of toxic shock syndrome, including fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

raw.rationale: The presence of purpuric retiform patches, rapid deterioration, and laboratory findings such as hyponatremia, neutropenia, and elevated liver enzymes are consistent with Purpura fulminans, a condition characterized by thrombosis and hemorrhagic necrosis of the skin.

rejected.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
rejected.why: Although Neisseria meningitidis can cause purpura, the Gram stain showing Gram-positive cocci does not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: While Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome can present with similar symptoms, the biopsy findings and Gram stain results are more indicative of Purpura fulminans

rejected.label: Meningococcemia
rejected.why: Meningococcemia typically presents with Neisseria meningitidis, which is a Gram-negative diplococcus, contradicting the Gram-positive cocci found in the tissue Gram stain

rejected.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically point towards Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome, and the presence of Gram-positive cocci in vessels could be consistent with Purpura fulminans
